summary: Comprehensive backend testing of Mindful Companion (FastAPI + MongoDB + httpOnly cookie JWT auth + real OpenAI gpt-5-mini via emergentintegrations). Created /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py with 50 pytest cases covering health, auth (register/login/me/logout/refresh + 401 enforcement on 17 endpoints), user settings (mode/voice), chat text + crisis detection + sessions + delete, mood logging + trends, journal CRUD + prompts, habits CRUD + completed_today + streak + toggle, breathing log, daily check-in (idempotent upsert), therapist summary, and crisis resources. All 50 tests pass.

minor.issue: Strict EmailStr rejects RFC reserved TLDs like *.test (422). Acceptable but worth noting for client-side guidance.
GET /api/breathing/sessions exists but is not documented in the feature list — fine, just FYI.

critical_code_review_comments: ai_service.synthesize_speech: TTS returns base64; if emergentintegrations API ever changes generate_speech_base64 signature this will silently break — wrap with logging (already done at caller).
chat/voice endpoint does not catch a generic exception around generate_chat_response (only logs not raise); a 500 with traceback would propagate. Minor robustness concern.
mood_trends, therapist_summary divide by len(moods) without guard inside avg_score expression — both endpoints already guard with `if moods` so OK; just keep eye if logic is later refactored.

CORS allow_origins defaults to '*' from env CORS_ORIGINS='*' WITH allow_credentials=True. Browsers will reject this combination; for production deployment set CORS_ORIGINS to explicit FRONTEND_URL. Currently tests via cookie jar work because they don't go through browser CORS.
Refresh-token endpoint sets both new access AND refresh tokens — a refresh-token rotation pattern is good; consider invalidating prior refresh on rotation to mitigate replay (acceptable for MVP).

Crisis detection uses keyword substring matching only ('hurt myself', 'suicide', etc.). Susceptible to false negatives (e.g., 'unalive') and false positives ('I want to die laughing'). Document as best-effort safety net, not primary safeguard.

Habit `streak` is computed as total count of completed logs, NOT consecutive-day streak as the field name suggests. This is a bug-level naming/semantics mismatch — either rename to `total_completions` or compute true consecutive-day streak.
No rate limiting / brute-force lockout on /auth/login (playbook recommends lockout after 5 fails). Not implemented — consider adding for production.
EMERGENT_LLM_KEY required at import time (os.environ['EMERGENT_LLM_KEY']) — fail-fast is fine but means tests cannot be run without the key in env.
test_credentials: admin@mindful.app / Admin@123 (verified working). Tests also auto-register fresh users with @example.com domain.
seed_data_creation: Admin user auto-seeded by backend startup (verified bcrypt hash starts with $2b$). Tests create per-module fresh users prefixed test_<uuid>@example.com plus TEST_ prefixed mood/journal/habit/checkin records.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py as regression suite. EmailStr rejects *.test/*.invalid TLDs — use @example.com. httpOnly cookie auth: requests.Session() automatically persists cookies across calls. Chat endpoint takes ~3-8s due to real gpt-5-mini call; timeout=90 used. Crisis detection works with keywords like 'kill myself'. Habit `streak` field semantics is a known bug (counts total completed logs, not consecutive days).
rca of the issue: No blocking issues. One semantic bug noted: habits[i].streak counts total completions instead of consecutive days. Fix: order completed logs by log_date desc, walk back day-by-day from today, break on gap.
